items.title: Cohere ships North Small Translate, an open-weight 218B model beating DeepL and Google Translate
items.summary: Cohere released North Small Translate on September 10, an open-weight sparse mixture-of-experts translation model (25B active / 218B total parameters, 128 experts with 8 active per token) covering 50 languages. It scores 83.6 on the WMT26 all-languages benchmark versus 81.37 for DeepL NextGen, rising to 84.36 with an agentic multi-pass mode that finds and fixes its own errors. It's text-only with a 16K-token input/output limit, weights gated on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0 for research and non-commercial use.
items.whyItMatters: A dedicated, openly-weighted translation model beating DeepL is a concrete building block for a "help me understand" translation fallback inside Romain or Anna, and its self-correcting agentic pass is a pattern worth studying for catching mistranslations before they reach a learner.

items.title: OpenAI pauses new $200 Pro sign-ups as Astra demand strains capacity
items.summary: OpenAI temporarily disabled new sign-ups and upgrades to its $200/month ChatGPT Pro tier on September 10, citing what a product lead called "unprecedented" demand for GPT-6 Astra's computer-use features straining infrastructure. Existing Pro subscribers are unaffected, and the API plus the Go and Plus plans remain open.
items.whyItMatters: A reminder that even OpenAI's own infrastructure can buckle under a popular agentic feature, worth factoring into capacity planning for any backend task that leans on GPT-6 Astra behind Romain.

items.title: Google launches a native Gemini desktop app for Windows
items.summary: Google shipped a native Gemini app for Windows 10 and 11 (x64 and ARM64) on September 10, invoked with an Alt+Space shortcut, with Workspace-grounded drafting from Gmail and Drive and built-in Nano Banana image generation. It's free with daily usage limits; heavier use requires a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription starting at $19.99/month.
items.whyItMatters: Not tutor-specific, but it's a data point on how Google is packaging an always-available assistant as an OS-level habit via one keyboard shortcut, the kind of frictionless entry point worth matching for Romain or Anna.

items.title: Sakana AI launches Fugu Max, an orchestration layer priced 40-60% below Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra
items.summary: Sakana AI released Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2 on September 11. Rather than a single trained network, Fugu is a multi-agent router that dispatches each task across a pool of open and specialized models, including Nvidia Nemotron, behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Priced at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens, Sakana says it undercuts Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Terra, and Kimi K3 on output cost while topping six agentic and coding benchmarks.
items.whyItMatters: A production example of routing each task to the cheapest capable model behind a single API is directly applicable to trimming backend costs for non-voice work, like grading or lesson generation, that supports Romain and Anna.
